summary: Rwanda is open to everyone: citizens of all African Union, Commonwealth and Francophonie states enter visa-free for 30 days, East African Community citizens stay up to six months, and every other nationality simply receives a 30-day visa on arrival (or applies online via Irembo).

passportValidity.text: Your passport or travel document must be valid for at least 6 months on the day you enter Rwanda.

vaccinations.name: Yellow fever
vaccinations.text: A yellow fever vaccination certificate is required if you arrive from a country with risk of yellow fever transmission.

source.name: Directorate General of Immigration and Emigration, Rwanda

travelInsurance.text: Insurance is not an entry requirement, but good private care is limited to Kigali — cover that includes medical evacuation is recommended, especially for trekking.

source.name: Directorate General of Immigration and Emigration, Rwanda

onwardTicket.text: Onward tickets are not routinely checked on arrival, but airlines may ask for one — carrying proof of return travel is sensible.

source.name: Directorate General of Immigration and Emigration, Rwanda

proofOfFunds.text: No fixed amount is published; immigration officers may ask visitors to show means of support for their stay.

source.name: Directorate General of Immigration and Emigration, Rwanda

currencyLimits.text: Cash of USD 10,000 or more (or the equivalent in other currencies) must be declared on arrival and departure.

source.name: Directorate General of Immigration and Emigration, Rwanda

notes: Non-biodegradable plastic bags are banned in Rwanda and are confiscated at the airport — pack with paper or cloth bags instead.

payments.text: Cards and mobile money are widely used in Kigali's hotels, restaurants and supermarkets; carry francs for markets, moto-taxis and rural areas.

safety.text: Rwanda is one of the safest countries in Africa, with low crime and clean, orderly cities. The main caution is the border zone with the DRC (and at times Burundi), where the regional security situation can change. Check advice before visiting Rubavu or crossing to Goma.

bestTimeToVisit.text: The long dry season from June to September is ideal for gorilla trekking and hiking; December to February offers a shorter dry window. The heaviest rains fall March to May.

idp.text: Rwanda is a party to the 1949 Geneva Convention on Road Traffic but not to the 1968 Vienna one, so the International Driving Permit it is bound to recognize is the 1949 Geneva version. A permit issued under the 1968 Vienna Convention carries no treaty obligation here.

driving.text: Rwanda is a party to the 1949 Geneva Convention on Road Traffic but not to the 1968 Vienna one, so the International Driving Permit it is bound to recognize is the 1949 Geneva version. A permit issued under the 1968 Vienna Convention carries no treaty obligation here. Whether a permit is required in addition to a national license, and for how long a foreign license may be used, are set by national road law and have not been checked for Rwanda yet.

tips.text: Gorilla-trekking permits for Volcanoes National Park cost USD 1,500 and sell out well ahead. Book months in advance through the Rwanda Development Board or a licensed operator.
Rwanda bans non-biodegradable plastic bags. They are searched for and confiscated on arrival. Repack duty-free and laundry into paper or cloth bags before you land.
On the last Saturday morning of each month (Umuganda), the country pauses for community work — shops stay shut and transport is limited until around midday.
Check current advice before traveling near the DRC border around Rubavu/Goma — cross-border tensions flare periodically even while the rest of Rwanda stays calm.
Visiting Kenya and Uganda on the same trip? The USD 100 East Africa Tourist Visa covers all three countries for 90 days. Apply through the country you enter first.

faq.question: Do I need a visa for Rwanda?
faq.answer: Entry is easy for everyone. Citizens of all African Union, Commonwealth and Francophonie member states enter visa-free for 30 days, East African Community citizens are admitted for up to six months, and every other nationality receives a 30-day visa on arrival (USD 50) with no advance application required.

faq.question: How does Rwanda's visa on arrival work?
faq.answer: All nationalities are eligible. At Kigali International Airport or any land border you pay USD 50 (cash or card) for a 30-day single-entry tourist visa. If you prefer, you can apply and pay in advance online through the official Irembo portal.

faq.question: What is the East Africa Tourist Visa?
faq.answer: A joint USD 100 visa valid 90 days for multiple entries across Kenya, Rwanda and Uganda. Apply through the country you will enter first — for Rwanda, via the Irembo portal — and enter that country before the others.

faq.question: Is Rwanda safe to visit?
faq.answer: Yes — Rwanda is widely regarded as one of Africa's safest destinations, and Kigali is clean and orderly with low crime. Stay informed about the border areas with the DRC and Burundi, where regional tensions can flare, and check travel advice before border excursions.

faq.question: Do I need a yellow fever vaccination for Rwanda?
faq.answer: Only if you arrive from a country with risk of yellow fever transmission — then the certificate is checked. It is still a sensible vaccination to have for a wider East African itinerary.

faq.question: Can I extend my stay in Rwanda?
faq.answer: Yes — visitor visas can be extended through the Directorate General of Immigration and Emigration (applications go through the Irembo portal) before your current stay expires. Apply a week or more ahead and be ready to show onward plans and means of support.
